content.thinking:
I'll import the Joint type and ColorInput, then start defining spine control points as coordinate arrays for the blade shape.

I'm sampling points along the blade path, computing the offset edge curve using a width function that peaks early (near the root) to mimic a classic scythe profile, then assembling outer and inner points into a closed outline while checking for self-intersection near the tip.

I'm also defining a sweep polyline for the glowing edge line, with a radius that tapers from base to tip and caps that are flat at the start and pointed at the end.

Now I'm adding the ribs as rod shapes extending from the outline points inward, positioned on either face of the spine with a tapering thickness, using a flat bone-tone paint to keep rendering costs down, then building the spine itself as a sweep along the same path.

I'm also planning smaller spine spikes branching off the main spine every few steps, computing their outward direction from the normal and tangent vectors, varying their length sinusoidally and tapering their radius toward the tip, anchored just off the spine surface.

Now I'm scattering tiny glow spheres along the spine at select intervals, then placing glyph planes along the blade at periodic positions, orienting them with the tangent and offsetting them outward using the scallop width, cycling through a few glyph textures for variety.

For the skull piece I'm setting up a helper that transforms local coordinates by the skull's orientation quaternion, then defining eye sockets as dark ellipsoids with small glowing eye cores positioned near the socket's front-facing surface.

I'm checking that the eye glow sits flush and slightly protruding past the socket, then adding a brow ridge capsule above each eye that overlaps the socket's upper edge for a hooded look, and I'm working out how the cranium's lateral width narrows at that z-depth so the eye and brow placements stay proportional.

Now I'm shaping the glowing orb at the chest with surrounding orbit rings, each torus angled differently to suggest a gyroscopic halo, plus a few small wisp cards near the mouth for a soul-breath effect, before moving on to the collar piece under the skull and neck.

Modeling the gold collar lathe and iron socket beneath it, then sketching out the short neck vertebra ring connecting up to the skull base, and starting a reusable bevelled ring function for the lower shaft ferrule geometry.

Now I'm working out the grip: sweeping a smooth cylindrical path for the handle and defining a wrapped paint function that alternates thread gold and leather colors based on helical pitch, adding some noise for a hand-painted feel, then placing a series of gold and dark iron decorative bands along the shaft at intervals.

I'm also designing the pommel's guard region with a layered iron and gold ring near the top, followed by a set of four curved claws radiating outward and downward using cubic bezier curves, colored with a bone gradient that darkens toward the tips.

Then I'm thinking through a charm chain hanging from the front, with a small gold eyelet torus attached to the iron ring, a chain of positioned links curving down the blade's face, and a gem-topped lantern piece at the chain's end.

The lantern needs a teal glowing octahedron gem, a gold cone cap above and spike below, four thin gold rods forming prongs around it, and finally some hanging tassel strands rendered as a small vertical-line SVG.

Now I'm building the spine's vertebrae loop, computing body radius tapering slightly over 14 segments, then adding spinous and transverse process spikes with bone coloring at each vertebra position.

I'm sizing the core glow tube to peek slightly beyond the vertebra radius so the discs read as glowing rings, then moving on to the plinth base shaped as an octagonal lathe.

Still working out the plinth geometry... I'm laying out the floor ring and rune ring annulus coordinates to sit between specific radii at the right height, making sure the outline points connect into a flat band around the plinth's upper step.

Now I'm planning the decorative elements: eight bone spikes ringing the first tier pointing outward and up, four claws built from bezier curves ending in bone and nail colors, and seven small crystal shapes scattered around a wider radius using octahedron and cone geometries.

I'm checking that the crystal bipyramids sink an acceptable amount into the base and applying random tilts and varied sizes to them. Then I'm placing wisp light cards oriented toward the viewer in a ring around the plinth top with slightly randomized sizes.

For the ghost cards I'm roughing out candidate positions near the blade's edge and deciding to alternate their depth placement rather than compute exact geometry yet. I'm also setting up the chain-based joint hinge for the charm, defining a four-point path with named segments, and assigning the eyelet to the shaft bone.

Now I'm sketching out mirrored symbol loops, the snout loft call with its station parameters, and a texture helper for generating SVG markup. For the ring texture I'm laying out a set of small rune-like glyph paths and planning to place them radially around the ring using rotation transforms, figuring out scale and stroke width for each glyph.

I'm scaling the glyphs so they read clearly within the ring's width, then designing the floor circle art with concentric rings (solid and dashed), tick marks, and hexagram polygons, mapping those SVG units back to real-world plinth and plane dimensions.

I'm placing hexagram triangles so their tips poke out beyond the plinth radius while staying hidden otherwise, adding small circles at r=86, and tallying up the texture atlas count across all the glyph, ring, floor, wisp, ghost, and tassel elements to confirm it fits. With glow and edge color settled, I'm moving into writing the actual build code, starting with flat shading for skull parts and the spike helper function signature for generating bone details.

Now I'm working out the options objects for rods, capsules, and lathe shapes, plus how rotation and bone binding work for torus rings and card frames so tassels and charms attach to the correct joints. I'm also sketching the paint function type signature and starting on the blade's edge-distance shader logic that measures how close a point is to the blade's edge polyline.

Writing paint shader logic...

Setting teeth color and now defining a banded horn paint function that alternates between two shaded tones based on position along the horn.

I'm shaping the horn as a curved bezier sweep with a tapering radius and a rounded-to-pointed cap, then adding two gold lathe rings along the horn's surface for decoration.

Next I'm planning smaller details: chin beard spikes under the jaw, dark narrow nostril shapes, and additional skull texture features.

Now I'm thinking through writing out the full creature file, making sure the jaw bone and its pose work with the mouth and tongue geometry—lofting a glowing teal tongue shape along stations down the jaw.

I'm checking whether the snout and jaw geometry might overlap when the mouth is closed, but since the jaw opens about 24 degrees there's enough clearance near the hinge; it's an acceptable amount of overlap. I'm working out the vertical placement of the upper teeth base relative to the snout bottom and the lower jaw's top edge to keep them from clipping badly.

I'm placing the neck as a capsule connecting the collar and skull, adding an iron yoke capsule and gold ring for blade root attachments, and deciding to skip extra shoulder plates on the bone structure for now.

Checking the texture parameter works for glyph planes with the up direction accepted properly. Tallying the part counts across skull, vertebrae, blade, and plinth, I'm landing around 300 total pieces, which feels solid, with room to add plinth scales later if needed.

Setting the base joint position and shaft orientation, I'm ready to write it.
